title: Vertical vs Horizontal Scaling
sources: DesignGurus, Grokking the System Design Interview, 'Horizontal vs Vertical Scaling': vertical scaling gives one machine more resources (more CPU cores, more memory, faster disks); there is a largest machine you can buy; a bigger server is still one server and a single point of failure; horizontal scaling adds more machines and spreads the work across them, usually behind a load balancer; very large systems are built this way

Zero To Mastery, 'Beginner's Guide to Horizontal vs Vertical Scaling' (2025-03-17): vertical = increasing CPU, RAM or storage, with a hardware ceiling; if the single upgraded server crashes everything goes down; horizontal = adding more machines to share the workload, needs something like a load balancer to distribute traffic

lines.text: and now one server can't keep up.
So do you get one bigger computer,
means giving your one chef a giant stove.
For servers, that's more CPU and memory.
Easy, but stoves only get so big,
and if that one chef gets sick,
means hiring more chefs who share the orders.
and it's how the biggest apps grow.
But wait, who hands out the orders?
